classification.difficultyReason: Project each graph onto both axes, distinguish attained extrema from asymptotic bounds, and express disconnected projections as unions. These are routine applications of the taught graph-reading methods, including non-function relations.

content.prompt: Identify the domain and range of these graphs.

spec.description: Increasing segment on ungridded Cartesian axes, with coordinate cues and two closed endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Closed endpoints (-2,-1) and (3,2).
spec.answerVisibility: No domain or range answer in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The graph covers $-2\le x\le3$ and $-1\le y\le2$. Both endpoints are closed, so both bounds are included.

Domain: $[-2,3]$. Range: $[-1,2]$.

spec.description: Increasing segment with an open lower-left endpoint and a closed upper-right endpoint; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Open (-2,-1), closed (3,2).
spec.answerVisibility: Question givens only.

answer.worked:
The open endpoint excludes $x=-2$ and $y=-1$. The closed endpoint includes $x=3$ and $y=2$.

Domain: $(-2,3]$. Range: $(-1,2]$.

spec.description: Increasing ray from a closed endpoint, continuing upwards and rightwards; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Closed initial point (-2,-1); x and y increase without bound.
spec.answerVisibility: Question givens only; no extra numeric endpoint labels.

answer.worked:
The closed starting point includes $x=-2$ and $y=-1$. The ray continues rightwards and upwards without bound.

Domain: $[-2,\infty)$. Range: $[-1,\infty)$.

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with two continuation arrows and a labelled closed vertex; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Vertex (-1/2,-2); unrestricted horizontal extent and minimum y=-2. Curve shape is schematic; no equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied vertex annotation remains visible.

answer.worked:
The parabola continues indefinitely to the left and right. Its lowest point is the included vertex at $y=-2$.

Domain: $\mathbb R$. Range: $[-2,\infty)$.

spec.description: Two disconnected increasing segments with every supplied coordinate cue; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Closed (-3,-1) to open (-1,1); closed (1,2) to closed (3,3).
spec.answerVisibility: Question givens only.

answer.worked:
The first segment covers $-3\le x<-1$ and $-1\le y<1$. The second covers $1\le x\le3$ and $2\le y\le3$. Join the separate intervals with $\cup$.

Domain: $[-3,-1)\cup[1,3]$.

Range: $[-1,1)\cup[2,3]$.

spec.description: Connected V-shaped segments with closed outer endpoints and labelled coordinate cues; no grid.
spec.mathematics: (-2,2) to (0,-1) to (2,2), including all three points.
spec.answerVisibility: Question givens only.

answer.worked:
The graph covers every $x$ from $-2$ to $2$. Its minimum is $y=-1$ and maximum is $y=2$, both included.

Domain: $[-2,2]$. Range: $[-1,2]$.

spec.description: Right-opening sideways parabola through the supplied vertex and y-axis crossings; two continuation arrows; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Vertex (-1,0), y-axis crossings (0,1) and (0,-1); x>=-1 and all real y.
spec.answerVisibility: Printed blue results are removed from the student diagram and stored in answers.

answer.worked:
The leftmost point is $x=-1$, which is included. The branches continue to the right, upwards and downwards without bound.

Domain: $[-1,\infty)$. Range: $\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Increasing straight line with arrows at both ends and labelled intercepts; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Intercepts (0,-1) and (2,0); line continues indefinitely.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied results appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
The line continues indefinitely in both directions, covering all real $x$-values and all real $y$-values.

Domain: $\mathbb R$. Range: $\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Vertical line distinct from the y-axis, with two continuation arrows and the x-value 2 labelled; no grid.
spec.mathematics: x=2 for every real y.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied domain and range results appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
Every point has $x=2$. The vertical line continues upwards and downwards without bound, so every real $y$-value occurs.

Domain: $\{2\}$. Range: $\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Two disconnected curves symmetric about the y-axis, with four continuation arrows; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Upper minimum (0,1), lower maximum (0,-1); both curves extend over all real x. Unspecified curves are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied blue results appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
The curves extend across all real $x$-values. The upper curve gives $y\ge1$ and the lower curve gives $y\le-1$, including both turning points.

Domain: $\mathbb R$.

Range: $(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$.

spec.description: Left-opening and right-opening disconnected curves, each with two continuation arrows and a labelled x-axis turning point; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Included turning points (-2,0) and (2,0); x<=-2 or x>=2, with every real y. Unspecified curves are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied results appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
The left branch covers $x\le-2$ and the right branch covers $x\ge2$. Both turning points are included. The branches extend upwards and downwards without bound.

Domain: $(-\infty,-2]\cup[2,\infty)$.

Range: $\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Reciprocal-shaped branches in quadrants I and III, approaching both axes with four continuation arrows; no grid or numeric labels.
spec.mathematics: Both coordinate axes are asymptotes; x=0 and y=0 are excluded. No function equation or scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied blue results appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
The branches approach the coordinate axes without touching them. Every nonzero $x$-value and every nonzero $y$-value occurs.

Domain: $(-\infty,0)\cup(0,\infty)$.

Range: $(-\infty,0)\cup(0,\infty)$.

spec.description: Upper semicircle with both axes arrowed at both ends, integer ticks and no grid or endpoint markers.
spec.mathematics: Upper semicircle centred at (0,0), radius 2; endpoints (-2,0) and (2,0), maximum (0,2).
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is a permanent given; domain and range responses are hidden in student mode.

answer.worked: The graph extends from $x=-2$ to $x=2$, including both endpoints. The domain is $[-2,2]$.
The lowest output is $0$ and the highest is $2$, both attained. The range is $[0,2]$.

spec.description: Complete unfilled ellipse centred at the origin; no grid or origin label. Horizontal axis has a right arrow and vertical axis an upward arrow. Ordinary curve and axes use house black.
spec.mathematics: Ellipse with horizontal intercepts (-3,0) and (3,0), and vertical intercepts (0,-2) and (0,2).
spec.answerVisibility: Ellipse and intercept labels remain visible; supplied domain and range appear only when answers are shown.

answer.worked: The horizontal shadow extends from $x=-3$ to $x=3$, including both extremes. The domain is $[-3,3]$.
The vertical shadow extends from $y=-2$ to $y=2$, including both extremes. The range is $[-2,2]$.

spec.description: Unfilled upward-opening parabola with vertex (3,1), arrows on both branches, positive-direction axis arrows, and dashed vertex-coordinate guides. No grid. The drawing coefficient controls schematic curvature and is not a supplied equation.
spec.mathematics: Vertex (3,1); extends indefinitely left and right; minimum y-value 1 is attained.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and coordinate labels remain visible; domain and range responses appear only when answers are enabled.

answer.worked: The branches extend indefinitely to the left and right, so every real input is allowed. Domain: $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
The vertex is the lowest point, at $y=1$, and the branches rise without bound. Since the minimum is included, the range is $[1,\infty)$.

spec.description: Unfilled sinusoidal curve with two peaks and two troughs, closed endpoints, positive-direction axis arrows and no grid.
spec.mathematics: The curve has the shape of y=sin(x) on [-2π,2π], crosses the origin while increasing, and attains y=-1 and y=1. Only endpoint x-values and the y-values -1 and 1 are labelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and axis labels remain visible; supplied domain and range appear only through response answers.

answer.worked: The graph extends from $x=-2\pi$ to $x=2\pi$, with both endpoints included, so the domain is $[-2\pi,2\pi]$. Its lowest and highest values are $y=-1$ and $y=1$, both attained, so the range is $[-1,1]$.

spec.sourceRegion: Middle row, centre cell, part q
spec.description: Increasing exponential-shaped curve above the x-axis, approaching it on the left, with arrows at both curve ends. Positive-direction axis arrows and x and y labels; no grid, numerical ticks or origin label.

answer.worked: The graph continues indefinitely to the left and right, so the domain is $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
The graph remains above the $x$-axis, approaches $y=0$ without reaching it, and increases without bound. The range is $(0,\infty)$.

spec.description: Increasing logarithmic-shaped curve entirely to the right of the y-axis, with a descending arrow near that axis and an upper-right continuation arrow. Axes have positive-direction arrows and x and y labels; there are no ticks, numbers, grid or printed formula.

answer.worked: The graph lies to the right of the $y$-axis and approaches it without reaching it, so $x>0$. Domain: $(0,\infty)$.
The curve continues downwards and upwards without bound, taking every real $y$-value. Range: $y\in\mathbb{R}$.

spec.description: Unshaded sideways oscillating relation with two left turns at x=-2, a right turn at (2,0), and filled endpoints at (2,3) and (2,-3). Positive-direction axis arrows; no grid.
spec.mathematics: The relation attains all x-values from -2 to 2 and all y-values from -3 to 3. The curve is reconstructed from its visible shape, not asserted to have a supplied equation.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source graph and coordinate labels are visible; supplied domain and range are stored in answers.

answer.worked: The graph reaches every $x$-value from $-2$ to $2$, including both extremes. Domain: $[-2,2]$.
The graph reaches every $y$-value from $-3$ to $3$. Both endpoints are filled, so both extremes are included. Range: $[-3,3]$.

spec.description: Unfilled black cubic-shaped curve, with a lower-left continuation arrow and an upper-right continuation arrow. Positive-direction axis arrows; labelled x-intercepts −1 and 1; no grid or vertical numerical labels.
spec.mathematics: The curve crosses the horizontal axis at −1, 0 and 1, has a local maximum to the left of the vertical axis and a local minimum to its right, and continues without bound in both directions. The plotted cubic is a qualitative reconstruction; no equation or vertical scale is asserted.

answer.worked: The graph continues indefinitely to the left and right, so every real input is allowed. Domain: $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
The continuous graph extends indefinitely downwards and upwards, so every real output occurs. Range: $y\in\mathbb{R}$.
